entries.title: Ising Model — modeling herd behavior and market phase transitions
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: 3D lattice visualization of the Ising model applied to financial markets. Blue=sellers, orange=buyers. At high volatility the market is random; as social pressure increases, clusters form leading to spontaneous symmetry breaking (crashes/trends). Built in Python for agent-based modeling.

entries.title: Phase Space Reconstruction — unfolding hidden BTC volatility dynamics
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Uses Phase Space Reconstruction (PSR) with time delay tau=3 to unfold BTCUSD volatility into a multi-dimensional manifold. Reveals whether market is in stable regime or chaotic transition. Key for quantitative regime detection.

entries.title: Heston Model — stochastic volatility for realistic options pricing
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Explains why Black-Scholes fails (constant vol assumption) and how the Heston Model introduces stochastic volatility. Captures the volatility smile and skew that basic models miss. Essential for options pricing.

entries.title: Cox Process — doubly stochastic Poisson for bursty market events
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Standard Poisson processes assume constant event rates, but markets are bursty. The Cox Process (Doubly Stochastic Poisson) uses a CIR-driven random intensity to model trade arrivals, defaults, and volatility spikes more realistically.

entries.title: Hidden Markov Models — detecting market regime shifts automatically
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Uses HMMs to mathematically deduce hidden market states from observable returns and volatility. Identifies low-vol bull, high-vol bear, and recovery regimes. Better than lagging indicators for strategy selection.

entries.title: Avellaneda-Stoikov — optimal spread calculation for market makers
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: The Avellaneda-Stoikov model solves the stochastic control problem for market making. Calculates optimal bid-ask spread based on volatility, time horizon, and inventory. Foundation of modern HFT market making. DM-bait for code repo.

entries.title: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Process — mean reversion for pairs trading
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Simulates the OU process showing mean reversion dynamics with theta (reversion speed), mu (equilibrium), and sigma (noise). Core model for pairs trading, interest rate spreads, and volatility signals in quantitative finance.

entries.title: Wave Function Collapse analogy — modeling pre-event price uncertainty
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Draws analogy between quantum wave function collapse and price discovery after news events. Pre-event price is a probability distribution; the event collapses it to a single reality. Emphasizes modeling uncertainty and tail risks for systematic trading.

entries.title: 3D Yield Curve Surface — visualizing cross-asset macro regimes
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: 3D visualization of yield curve dynamics across macro regimes: COVID-19 vol shock (VIX spike, yield compression), Fed tightening cycle (curve inversion). Shows how Treasury yield warping drives cross-asset correlations.

entries.title: Volatility Surface — regime shifts from smile to smirk
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: 3D visualization of implied volatility surface (moneyness x maturity x IV). Shows how the surface warps from gentle 'smile' to steep 'smirk' before tail-risk events as markets bid up OTM puts for downside protection.

entries.title: Omori's Law — earthquake aftershock math applied to market crashes
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Applies geophysics' Omori's Law to financial markets. Post-crash volatility aftershocks decay at a predictable rate following power-law dynamics, not randomly. Shows March 2020 crash decay pattern. DM-bait for code repo.

entries.title: Wasserstein Distance — measuring the backtest-to-live reality gap
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Uses Wasserstein Distance and Sinkhorn Divergence to mathematically measure drift between backtest distributions (blue) and live market conditions (orange). Detects distribution shift that kills more strategies than bad fees.

entries.title: Singular Spectrum Analysis — non-parametric trend extraction from noisy data
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: SSA decomposes time-series into trend, cycles, and noise without assuming a fixed functional form. Breaks data into reconstructed components (RC 1+7 trend, RC 2+3 annual, RC 9 high-freq). DM-bait for code repo.

entries.title: Lempel-Ziv Complexity — compression algorithms to detect market predictability
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Applies the LZ compression algorithm (behind .zip files) to financial time series. When LZ complexity is low, patterns repeat and the market is more predictable. When high, it's random noise. Novel cross-domain application.

entries.title: Fast Fourier Transform — decomposing NVDA price into frequency signals
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Applies FFT to NVDA price action to decompose it into frequency components, separating noise from dominant cycles. Shows how to identify the strongest periodic signals in price data.

entries.title: Monte Carlo — 25,000 shuffled BTC returns to separate edge from luck
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Runs 25,000 Monte Carlo simulations by shuffling daily BTC-USD returns to test whether a strategy's performance is genuine edge or statistical luck. One backtest isn't enough — real quants demand statistical significance.

entries.title: Minimum Spanning Tree — graph theory reveals S&P 500 hidden structure
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Applies graph theory (Minimum Spanning Tree) to the S&P 500 to map the hidden network structure between stocks. Reveals sector clusters and systemic risk connections that traditional correlation matrices obscure. DM-bait for code.

entries.title: Avalanche Model — self-organized criticality explains market crashes
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Markets reach self-organized criticality where small perturbations trigger cascading failures. The 'news' doesn't cause the crash — the system was already at a critical state. Applies sandpile/avalanche dynamics from physics to explain market fragility.

entries.title: Tick Data vs OHLC — you're trading on 0.002% of available data
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Daily OHLC candles compress ~86,400 seconds of market data into 4 numbers — throwing away 99.998% of information. Makes the case for tick-level and limit order book analysis over candle-based trading.

entries.title: Lyapunov Exponent — measuring chaos in BTC tick-level microstructure
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Visualizes the Lyapunov Exponent of BTC-USD microstructure data. Positive exponent = chaotic/unpredictable, negative = deterministic. Reveals that what looks random on 5-min charts has measurable chaotic structure at tick level.

entries.title: Kalman Filter — adaptive signal extraction for non-stationary markets
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Financial data is non-linear and non-stationary, breaking standard filters. Kalman Filter adapts in real-time, unlike lagging moving averages or FFT (which assumes stationarity). Optimal for real-time signal extraction.

entries.title: Continuous Wavelet Transform — time-frequency analysis of QQQ
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Applies CWT to QQQ to analyze frequency-domain dynamics over time. Unlike FFT (fixed window), wavelets capture how dominant frequencies shift across regimes. Reveals the market's changing 'heartbeat'.

entries.title: Random Matrix Theory — cleaning correlation matrices from noise
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Standard correlation matrices treat random noise as valid connections. Random Matrix Theory (RMT) filters eigenvalues to 'clean' the matrix, keeping only statistically significant correlations. The market is 90% noise.

entries.title: Stable Distribution — modeling fat-tailed crashes beyond Gaussian
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Markets go up slowly but crash fast. Standard Gaussian models underestimate crash probability. Uses Stable (Levy) distributions to properly model fat tail events and Black Swan risks that beginners ignore.

entries.title: Hurst Exponent — 3D surface of BTC memory and mean-reversion zones
entries.creator: quant.dhawan
entries.summary: Plots the Hurst Exponent of BTC-USD as a 3D surface. H>0.5 = trending (momentum), H<0.5 = mean-reverting, H=0.5 = random walk. Shows how market 'memory' varies across timeframes. Basis for adaptive strategy selection.

entries.title: REA MCP — agent-driven reverse engineering with a Ghidra backend
entries.creator: backsla.sh
entries.summary: REA is an MCP server that lets an AI agent reverse engineer apps and stripped native binaries, with Ghidra doing the decompilation while the agent drives and cites evidence per call. The creator decompiled a closed-source program in three to four minutes on Ubuntu. Setup is deferred to a follow-up video.

entries.title: Claude Opus 5.5 to Blender — 3D animation built entirely as code
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: Claude Opus 5.5 wrote everything: a web mock of the After Effects UI, a Python script that builds the Blender scene, the character animation, plus the music and sound effects. Blender rendered 360 frames on GPU in about 15 minutes and FFmpeg stitched the video. Full prompt is comment-gated.

entries.title: Mandelbulb — ray-marching a 3D fractal from z⁸ + c
entries.creator: elemental.math
entries.summary: Explains the Mandelbulb: Daniel White's spherical-coordinate trick for 3D 'multiplication', raised to power 8 by Paul Nylander, rendered by ray marching with the distance estimate d = ½·r·log r/dr. Code is ported line by line from Mandelbulber's GPL-3.0 source, with the Hamilton 'multiply triplets' history as a bonus.

entries.title: CoreWeave debt explained — how GPU-backed loans fund the neoclouds
entries.creator: thewallstreetskinny
entries.summary: An ex-Morgan Stanley CDO structurer explains the neocloud stack (landlords, vertically integrated players like IREN and Crusoe, CoreWeave, Nebius) and why CoreWeave's GPU-backed asset financing spooked markets. Advance rates hit 90-95% against off-taker credit, and loan, contract and GPU useful life are nearly the same length, leaving a thin tail.

entries.title: Block Blast reverse-engineered — on-device XGBoost rigs difficulty for ad revenue
entries.creator: ayoships
entries.summary: A reverse engineer found Block Blast runs a local XGBoost model on device signals (phone model, country, past ad revenue, vibration setting) to predict your ad value and adjust difficulty. Rules like 'Boost Then Kill' and 'High Value Ad Harvest' trigger a 'death algorithm' right when a pricey revive ad is ready. Full code evidence is promised later on the creator's site.

entries.title: Claudex skill — Claude and GPT-6 Astra cross-audit plan and build
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: A free skill that splits work between two frontier models: Claude writes the plan and GPT-6 Astra audits it until it holds, then roles swap so Astra builds and Claude audits. Runs inside Claude or Codex as a reusable skill.

entries.title: Headless software + MCP — Chamath on why software IP stops being a moat
entries.creator: atlasberry008
entries.summary: Breaks down Chamath's All-In claim that software IP is worthless once services go headless and agents call them via MCP. With Salesforce and xAI's Grok exposing headless engines, agents pick tools on speed, cost or accuracy, so the interface stops being the moat.

entries.title: Qwen 27B at home — a dev ditching frontier labs for local models
entries.creator: cjtrowbridge
entries.summary: An ex-lab engineer argues the free Qwen 27B model, run locally or in the cloud, handles long complex tasks better than frontier labs. Also claims Blackwell chips, including their Jetson Thor boxes, have broken speculative decoding. Opinion-heavy with strong unverified claims.

entries.title: Reverse Engineer Anything — trending repo that explains how any app works
entries.creator: theericmichaud
entries.summary: The week's top trending GitHub repo, about 70k stars: point Claude Code or Codex at an app and it explains how the feature is built so you can rebuild it. Users have revived old hardware, e.g. a Logitech keypad on Linux in 15 minutes, plus scanners and sound cards that lost drivers.

entries.title: Game decompilation with AI — which reconstruction methods stay legal
entries.creator: lizthedeveloper
entries.summary: Covers five decompilation approaches (matching decompilation, functional reconstruction, static recompilation, engine re-implementation, porting recovered source) and argues engine re-implementation and functional reconstruction are the legal paths. AI fits because the original game's GPU pixel output is a verifiable oracle for rewriting the engine in a new language.

entries.title: Tencent WorldClaw — prompt-to-3D worlds with every object a separate asset
entries.creator: mr.eflow
entries.summary: Tencent's WorldClaw generates a whole 3D scene from a prompt where every tree, house and lamp post is an editable mesh. It chains image generation (GPT Image 2), Segment Anything to split objects, and Hunyuan 2D-to-3D, with depth, normal and instance maps. Not publicly available yet.

entries.title: Open-source AI week — OpenViking, ARTEMIS, GLM-5.3 FlashX, Unsloth Studio
entries.creator: drcintas
entries.summary: Six releases in 60 seconds: OpenViking (context database for agent memory), Google's ARTEMIS (prompt-to-phone automation over MCP for Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity), PrismML Ternary Bonsai 2 (27B ternary reasoning model, 262k context), AWS Pizza Bot (email-style inbox for background agents), Z.ai GLM-5.3 FlashX (320B multimodal, 1M context, local), and Unsloth Studio no-code fine-tuning of 500+ models in free Colab.

entries.title: DuckStation 3D screenshot — rip any PS1 scene to OBJ for Blender
entries.creator: rosamichael.digital
entries.summary: A DuckStation fork with a 3D-screenshot feature dumps the current PS1 scene as an OBJ with positions intact, ready to drag into Blender. More reliable than the older Avocado emulator route, which had vertex and texture bugs. The creator turns rips into papercraft models.

entries.title: Open vs closed token share — Friedberg on the 12-week flip and Anthropic risk
entries.creator: techno.optimist.prime
entries.summary: David Friedberg on All-In says token usage flipped from 80/20 closed-to-open to 80/20 open-to-closed in 12 weeks, calling it Anthropic's biggest risk factor ahead of S-1s. He expects a bifurcated market: open weights for most use, premium models for hard engineering, math and biology work.

entries.title: ln + vpype — 3D scenes to hidden-line vector art for pen plotters
entries.creator: index.opensource
entries.summary: Michael Fogleman's ln (Go) renders 3D scenes as 2D vector paths by ray-testing each path segment for visibility, supporting CSG, math surfaces and procedural cities. vpype then merges and sorts paths for plotting, cutting pen-up travel 86% in this example. Both MIT licensed, output straight to SVG.

entries.title: Quake III fast inverse square root — the 0x5f3759df bit hack explained
entries.creator: mygearhut
entries.summary: Explains Quake III's four-line fast inverse square root: reinterpret float bits as an integer (which behaves logarithmically), shift right to halve the exponent, subtract from magic constant 0x5f3759df, then one Newton-Raphson step to bring error under 0.175%. Covers why normalization was costly on 1999 Pentiums and the constant's lineage through 3dfx and Cleve Moler.

entries.title: AI game decompilation hype — Mario/Halo merges and PS5 piracy rumors

Agents commit under their own names and can be messaged mid-task, and they walk over to find you when they need input.

entries.title: Self-improving trading agent — critic loop that rewrites losing strategies

Hard-coded stop-loss and drawdown limits sit outside the agent's reach, and failed strategies go to a local DB the agent learns from. Guide is comment-gated.

entries.creator: ryanlpeterman
entries.summary: Casey Muratori argues Conway's law is software's only real law: once you split work among workers (people or agents) whose communication is slower than their internal compute, design iteration across that boundary is locked in as slower. 'Products look like the org chart' is a consequence, not the law itself.

entries.title: GENIUS Act stablecoins — how banks keep the T-bill yield on your cash
entries.creator: alexanderelorenzo
entries.summary: Under the GENIUS Act banks can issue stablecoins, park the backing cash in short-term Treasury bills, keep the roughly 4% yield (the law bars passing it to holders), and repo the T-bills for liquidity. Holders can swap into tokenized Treasuries like USYC, which Binance accepts as collateral. Ends with a paid-group pitch.

entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Method behind the viral AI monk marketing: find a trending person or format, generate a stylized Pixar-like character instead of a deceptive likeness, write an ironic script that features your product, record your own dialogue, then generate shots from a beat list and edit. The creator admits it took heavy refinement.

entries.title: Expired-domain rebuild — a black-hat SEO backlink tactic
entries.creator: edward.builds
entries.summary: Buy a relevant expired domain, rebuild it from the Wayback Machine, force-index with IndexChex, prop it up with cheap niche edits, then add one contextual link to your site once it ranks and push paid traffic through it. Requires footprint hiding (separate emails, hosting, IPs). Explicitly black-hat with penalty risk.

entries.title: Katana crawler — fast JS endpoint and API route discovery for web recon
entries.creator: declan.middleton
entries.summary: ProjectDiscovery's Katana crawls web apps to surface endpoints, URLs, parameters and JavaScript files, prioritizing JS endpoints and API routes. Demoed on Kali Linux against a lab VM. Use only on systems you are authorized to test.

entries.title: Workflow hijacking — Noma research on AI automations with no authorization
entries.creator: mattjayy
entries.summary: Noma Labs research shows AI workflows (email auto-responders, GitHub Actions, Google email flows) leak data when an attacker simply asks, because nothing checks whether the requester is authorized. Not prompt injection, the model is doing what it's told. The fix is bringing identity and authorization into agent workflows.

entries.title: Higgsfield plugin for ChatGPT — floor plans to 3D walkthroughs with GPT-6 Astra
entries.creator: chandlerintelligence
entries.summary: Sponsored Higgsfield post claiming GPT-6 Astra plus the Higgsfield ChatGPT plugin turns floor plans into 3D walkthroughs, builds playable games and makes motion graphics. No transcript content survives beyond the caption.

entries.title: Subscription token arbitrage — Claude Max vs Grok Ultra API-equivalent usage
entries.creator: duck.tate
entries.summary: Compares plan value: Claude's $200 Max is worth over $7,000/month in API usage, while Grok Ultra at $300 is claimed at over $12,000. The creator plans to switch from Claude as brain plus Codex as hands to Fable as brain plus Grokbot as hands.

entries.title: Data reclamation game — gamifying opt-outs from data brokers
entries.creator: lizthedeveloper
entries.summary: A developer built a game to make reclaiming your personal data from corporations and data brokers as engaging as signing up was, countering dark-pattern cancellation flows. Mostly framing, few specifics on which opt-outs it covers.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra + Higgsfield — cabin photos to a walkable 3D game world
entries.creator: mr.paidsocial
entries.summary: Sponsored Higgsfield showcase of GPT-6 Astra feats (one-shot games, Unreal NPCs each with their own Astra brain, Blender scenes), ending with photos of a real cabin turned into a walkable first-person 3D world via the Higgsfield plugin in ChatGPT.

entries.title: Fable orchestrates, Opus executes — cutting frontier-model token spend
entries.creator: thomas.lentine
entries.summary: Brain-dump your task list to Fable, have it write specs and spawn cheaper Opus subagents (in parallel worktrees) to execute, then Fable reviews and sends fixes back in a loop until it's good enough. You get top-model judgment without burning usage limits on implementation.

entries.title: Shared second-brain MCP — team access to ICM context folders across AIs
entries.creator: lostandlucky
entries.summary: A team built an MCP server for their context-sharing platform so any AI can list and read shared ICM templates (folder-based LLM wikis with instructions and scripts) without logging in or syncing via GitHub, SharePoint or zip files. New uploads from teammates show up immediately.

entries.title: Reddit OSINT tool — recover deleted posts and comments by username
entries.creator: declan.middleton
entries.summary: A Reddit OSINT search tool surfaces posts and comments tied to a username, including ones deleted years ago, by drawing on archived data. Demo is light and ends with a community pitch. Use responsibly and lawfully.

entries.title: Manus-sponsored vibe-coding teaser — no content
entries.creator: natashabuilds
entries.summary: A Manus paid-partnership clip teasing a 'cheat code for vibecoding' with no spoken or on-screen content captured.

entries.title: MapQuest MCP for Claude — location-aware agents that route your day
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: Plugging the MapQuest MCP server into Claude gives the model real place search, distances, travel times and traffic, so it can order a day's stops into a sensible route instead of listing random recommendations. Same server works for any agent that needs geography; MapQuest offers 50,000 free transactions to start.

entries.title: PostHog interest-segmented landing pages — personalize by visitor behavior
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Sponsored PostHog post: install PostHog, let two weeks of visitor sessions accumulate, then prompt an AI to cluster visitors into interest groups (e.g. sales vs. support features) and generate a landing-page variant per group that returning visitors see. Also argues flashy animated landing templates convert poorly.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra + Codex one-person company — context files and daily checkpoints
entries.creator: raycfu
entries.summary: Set up a workspace with three markdown context files (aboutme.md built from a 20-question interview, an anti-AI writing-style ban list, and mycompany.md with model, revenue and quarterly goals), then run Codex on GPT-6 Astra at three daily checkpoints: 8am inbox triage and call prep, noon delegation to sub-agents, 5pm audit whose summary seeds tomorrow's context.

entries.title: Katana crawler — JavaScript endpoint discovery and deep-crawl flags
entries.creator: declan.middleton
entries.summary: Part two of a Katana walkthrough: use the JavaScript-crawl flag to pull endpoints out of JS files that a basic crawl misses, set crawl depth with -d, and write results to a file. Demoed against a local CTF VM; only for systems you own or are authorized to test.

entries.title: NFC stickers + vibe-coded web app — physical taps that log real-life habits
entries.creator: byjackprice
entries.summary: Programmable NFC stickers on a water bottle trigger an Apple Shortcut that logs each finished bottle to a tiny Next.js/TypeScript web app, surfaced as a home-screen widget. Part two of an IRL vibe-coding series; next step is a Raspberry Pi force sensor to log automatically.

entries.title: Overnight return anomaly — most stock gains accrue close-to-open
entries.creator: eliteoptionstrader2
entries.summary: Cites research showing that across global markets most equity returns come overnight (close to next open) while intraday holding loses; the Micron example claims +138M% overnight vs −99% intraday on paper. Proposed mechanism: retail trades the open, institutions trade into the close. Paper not named; frictions and costs ignored.

entries.title: x402 protocol — pay-per-crawl tolls for AI agents scraping your site
entries.creator: alexanderelorenzo
entries.summary: Frames the AI scraping lawsuits (Anthropic's ~$1.5B author settlement, NYT v. OpenAI) as a payment problem and points to x402, a 2025 protocol that revives the long-dormant HTTP 402 Payment Required status so agents pay a crypto micropayment to access content. Explanation is hype-heavy and ends in a paid Skool pitch.

entries.title: AI Overview SEO — seeding social posts that Google and ChatGPT cite
entries.creator: edward.builds
entries.summary: A LinkedIn post declaring someone 'the world's most renowned AI visibility expert' was cited by Google's AI Overview the same day. Lesson: user-generated platforms (YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn, X) dominate citations, so lead posts with your keyword and backlink them to keep them cited. Ends in a promo for compactkeywords.com.

entries.title: Microduck robot — reinforcement learning with PPO and reward shaping
entries.creator: summerr.exe
entries.summary: Training Pollen Robotics' open-source Microduck to stand: define a reward function (e.g. points for target body height), simulate 4,096 parallel robots, and let PPO update the policy toward higher-reward actions. The result 'stands' in an unintended way, a clean demo of reward hacking and why reward design is iterative.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra prompt pack — comment-bait with no content
entries.creator: tenfoldmarc
entries.summary: Caption teases GPT-6 Astra prompts for Codex/ChatGPT behind a comment keyword; the audio is just music, so the post carries no actual prompts or technique.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra stock-trading challenge — scheduled Codex tasks in one thread
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: Creator gives GPT-6 Astra $10k to trade, rerunning an earlier Claude experiment that reportedly beat the S&P by 8% in a month. Six scheduled Codex tasks per day read news, open, review and manage positions, all posting into one shared thread for visibility. No results yet; setup doc gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Herk Brain AI OS — local knowledge graph wired into a personal dashboard
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: A local folder-based 'AI operating system' links business wiki, meetings, video knowledge, Claude/Codex memory, projects, skills and agents into one graph, then exposes it through a personal OS dashboard (calendar, Slack/ClickUp/email replies, meeting action items, YouTube comment trends). A free GitHub repo interviews you and scaffolds the same setup, 3D brain view included.

entries.title: Stay-secure privacy checklist — de-dox yourself from AI and data brokers
entries.creator: lizthedeveloper
entries.summary: After Meta AI pieced together a creator's home location from old posts, this free browser-only checklist walks you through mapping your accounts, auditing what's public, opting out of data brokers and ad trackers, credit freezes, recovery codes, tracking who holds your ID, and identity-theft recovery.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra web design skill — layered parallax hero sections in one shot
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: Showcase of one-shot landing pages from GPT-6 Astra using the creator's design skill: multi-layer parallax scroll scenes, 3D product elements that morph on scroll, minimal premium sections below. Visual reference only; the skill is gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Three cybersecurity portfolio projects — fuzzing, agent sandboxing, YARA scanning
entries.creator: carterperez.dev
entries.summary: Portfolio ideas that signal real skill: a fuzzer that hammers C libraries with malformed files to find memory-corruption crashes; an AI agent guard that assumes prompt injection will succeed and limits what the agent may do; and a static binary scanner that matches detection rules and explains each hit. Source links gated behind a comment.

entries.title: ChatGPT warm-referral job hunt — mutual connections to bypass ATS filters
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Sponsored ChatGPT post: have ChatGPT find the recruiter and hiring manager for a role, list your mutual connections in a spreadsheet, message those contacts asking to use their name, then run a scheduled task that drafts a name-drop email to the hiring manager when they say yes.

entries.title: UX laws cheat sheet — 20 rules to feed Claude as design instructions
entries.creator: adam_ha_yes
entries.summary: Rapid list of UX principles meant to be dropped into a markdown instruction file for Claude: fewer choices per screen, large targets, familiar patterns, chunking, sub-400ms response, clear primary action, visible progress, sensible defaults, error prevention and recovery, progressive disclosure, and goal-gradient framing.

entries.title: Four GitHub design repos — R3F, liquid glass, shader gradients, liquid chrome
entries.creator: cindie.zhu
entries.summary: Treat GitHub as a designer's asset library: React Three Fiber for Three.js 3D, liquid-glass-js for Apple-style liquid glass, ShaderGradient for animated customizable gradients in React, and Liquid Logo for a chrome liquid-metal effect. Point Claude Code or Codex at a repo, check licence and maintenance, and adapt the smallest effect in a throwaway branch.

entries.title: MLS API rental finder — bypass Zillow with your own listings pipeline
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Get MLS data via API by registering as a vendor sponsored by a realtor friend, then prompt an AI to build a workflow that pulls listings matching your filters into your own database and emails each listing agent to express interest. Idea credited to another builder.

entries.title: Soup — fine-tune LLMs on a 4GB laptop GPU with one command
entries.creator: martintrainhard
entries.summary: Soup, built by a 17-year-old solo founder from Kazakhstan, wraps LLM fine-tuning into a simple flow: describe the goal, point at your data, run `soup train`, and it auto-picks batch size and memory settings. Claimed 85k users training medical assistants and reasoning models on consumer GPUs. Link gated; verify the claims.

entries.title: Gestural agent interface — TouchDesigner concept for hand-commanded AI
entries.creator: the.poet.engineer
entries.summary: Non-functional TouchDesigner prototype imagining agentic UI driven by gestures: two running fingers run the program, spinning fingers spin up a new idea, a pinch delegates heavy lifting.

entries.title: ARRAY circular edition — TouchDesigner light-art process
entries.creator: perspek.steven
entries.summary: Process glimpse from perspek.steven's ARRAY series: a circular light-art piece built and sequenced in TouchDesigner. Silent visual reference for generative lighting and new-media installation work.

entries.title: Bending Spoons playbook — AI-native acquisitions of stagnant SaaS
entries.creator: tom__shipley
entries.summary: Bending Spoons grew from $40k to an $18B IPO by buying stagnating platforms (Evernote, Vimeo, Meetup, WeTransfer) cheaply, rebuilding only the core features customers use with a lean elite engineering team, cutting cost base and compounding margin into the next deal. Argues AI-native acquirers, not vendors, are the new playbook PE/VC is funding.

entries.title: Booking.com AI observability — Kafka buffer and PII redaction before Arize
entries.creator: therobertta
entries.summary: Walkthrough of Booking.com's GenAI telemetry architecture: apps emit traces to a collector, which normalizes them onto a managed Kafka bus (durable buffer decoupling producers and consumers), through a dedicated PII-redaction service that masks span attributes and text, then out to Arize for real-time monitoring and a warehouse for offline analytics and backfills. A second pipeline ships ML prediction logs to Arize for ranking and fraud models.

entries.title: Six monetizable AI GitHub repos — clipping, Remotion, OpenHands and more
entries.creator: raycfu
entries.summary: Side-income angles for six open-source repos: AutoClip for auto-cutting highlights from long videos, Remotion for templated programmatic video, OpenHands as an autonomous software developer to package for SMBs, PersonaLive for real-time AI avatar livestreams, RedInk for Xiaohongshu (RedNote) text+image content, and MuMu AI Novel for bulk fiction writing.

entries.title: PostHog reader-drop analytics — AI feedback loop for human writers
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Argues AI-written articles all come out the same, so hire a human writer, install PostHog on the blog, and have an AI agent analyze scroll and read-through data on each article to tell the writer where and why readers dropped off, iterating every piece. Framed as a 'PostHog appreciation post', likely sponsored.

entries.title: Gausseous — free browser tool for audio-reactive Gaussian splat visuals
entries.creator: dave_bewick
entries.summary: Open-source, browser-based Gaussian splat manipulator: load 3DGS scans and add audio reactivity, depth of field, lens curvature, swirly bokeh, film emulation, quantisation and render export, no plugins or TouchDesigner needed. Built with World Labs' SparkJS and help from Claude Code; works on desktop and phones.

entries.title: Vertus Neurotopology — sponsored AI-trading claims dressed as news
entries.creator: stics.ai
entries.summary: Carousel sponsored by Vertus: opens with a Claude Fable 5 Polymarket BTC dashboard and a TradingView-via-MCP backtest demo, dismisses transformer models as 'pattern matchers' using a live-capital benchmark, then pitches Vertus' 'Neurotopology' architecture with 51.15% 2025 returns and 2.13 Sharpe sourced from a paid EZ Newswire press release. Treat as an ad.

entries.title: Alien's Eye — username OSINT search across social platforms
entries.creator: declan.middleton
entries.summary: Alien's Eye searches a username across many social and web platforms (even Khan Academy, Google Classroom) and lists matching profile links, pitched as better than Sherlock. Use it on your own handles to find forgotten accounts.

entries.title: Self-improving skills vs AI teammates — log issues, rewrite skills
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Argues personified 'AI teammates' are static while skills are adaptable: keep every skill in a database table, have each skill log issues about itself when used into a second table, then periodically run a prompt that reads the accumulated issues and rewrites the skill. Specific workflows with clear end states beat persona prompts.

entries.title: God's Eye View — open-source 3D geospatial OSINT globe with voice agent
entries.creator: bilawal.ai
entries.summary: Bilawal Sidhu open-sourced God's Eye View V1 (MIT): a browser 3D globe tracking real-time planes, ships, satellites, traffic cameras and infrastructure, with FLIR-style modes, a voice agent you can ask what's happening, annotations, and cockpit views. Extend it with new data layers.

entries.title: Xiaomi AI Cube — 80GB unified-memory box running 120B models locally
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: Xiaomi showed a prototype AI Cube with 80GB unified memory running 3B and 120B models on-device, built on three in-house chips: XRING O3 (mobile), O100 AI accelerator (claimed 1.22 TB/s near-memory bandwidth) and D100 3nm driving chip. No price, release date or independent benchmarks yet.

entries.title: Mail Access — terminal OSINT tool for investigating email addresses
entries.creator: declan.middleton
entries.summary: Quick demo of an OSINT command-line tool that investigates an email address, harvesting related emails and organization addresses by crawling. Thin walkthrough; ends with a Skool pitch.

entries.title: Cursor 'Grok Bot' source-map leak — readable agent runtime rewired to any model
entries.creator: stridejosh.ai
entries.summary: Claims Cursor shipped its $200-300/month agent with source maps enabled, exposing the TypeScript coordinator, execution daemons and protocol; the community restored it (minus front end) and rewired it to run Claude Code, Codex or OpenRouter models. Compares it to Claude Code's March source-map leak and DMCA takedowns. Archive gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Microsoft SkillOpt — agent skills that rewrite themselves against benchmarks
entries.creator: marc.kaz
entries.summary: Microsoft open-sourced SkillOpt: a base model runs a task, an optimizer rewrites the skill instructions from results, successful paths are separated from failures, and edits that don't beat the benchmark are auto-rejected. Claimed to beat hand-written prompts and TextGrad and to transfer across models.

entries.title: Build-your-own CLI for agents — control apps that lack an MCP
entries.creator: catlabs
entries.summary: When a program has no MCP server or the MCP misses controls you need, tell the agent 'Build yourself a CLI tool to interact with [program]', even down to every button of a DAW. MCP stays best for auth, discovery and distribution; a custom CLI wins for bespoke complex workflows and uses fewer tokens. Expect security flags.

entries.title: Google Ad Grants — $10k/month for nonprofits and the $2 CPC workaround
entries.creator: pat.berlinquette
entries.summary: 501(c)(3) nonprofits can get $10,000/month in Google Ads indefinitely; the creator claims compliance rules (quality score, single-word keywords, 5% CTR) are barely enforced, and that switching from manual CPC to Maximize Conversions with imported GA4 micro-conversions lets campaigns bid past the $2 CPC cap.

entries.title: only-cli/oc — browse websites as a compact numbered CLI for agents
entries.creator: githubsignals
entries.summary: Open-source tool that fetches a page and returns a tidy numbered text view so agents can read, follow links and search for hundreds of tokens instead of tens of thousands of raw HTML; mimics a real browser to slip basic blocks. Spotted on Hacker News.

entries.title: Backpropagation visualized — gradients as downhill steps on the loss surface
entries.creator: techvrix
entries.summary: Welch Labs explainer clip: estimate how loss changes per parameter (e.g. nudging m2 from 0 to 0.1 drops loss from 2.45 to 2.24), combine all partial derivatives into the gradient, and step against it; backprop uses the chain rule to compute that gradient efficiently across the network.

entries.title: Three OPSEC tools — text steganography, P2P file send, MAC spoofing
entries.creator: carterperez.dev
entries.summary: Teaser for three privacy tools: hide an encrypted message inside normal-looking text, send a file laptop-to-laptop with no cloud where the link dies when the app closes, and randomize your MAC address in one command. Tool names gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Artist statement formula — what you make, how and why, why it matters
entries.creator: keshabruce
entries.summary: From 20 years on grant and fellowship panels: an artist statement only needs three things: what you make, how and why you make it, and why it matters. If you can't explain the ideas, galleries, grants and residencies won't take you seriously. One-hour template gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Awesome Systematic Trading — curated quant libraries, models and backtesters
entries.creator: wadoodai
entries.summary: Awesome Systematic Trading is a free, curated GitHub list of Python libraries, quantitative models, backtesting frameworks and execution tutorials for building automated trading and risk pipelines locally. Hype framing aside, it is a solid map of the open-source quant stack.

entries.title: MoneyPrinterTurbo — one-topic-in, finished short video out
entries.creator: franklim.gui
entries.summary: Portuguese walkthrough of MoneyPrinterTurbo, a top-trending GitHub repo: give it a topic and it writes the script, pulls HD/4K stock footage, adds narration, subtitles and music, and renders vertical or horizontal videos in batches. Works with Claude, DeepSeek, ChatGPT and Gemini; runs locally or via Google Colab, no watermark.

entries.title: Moderna–Merck personalized mRNA cancer therapy — first positive Phase 3
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: Moderna and Merck reported the first positive Phase 3 result for an individualized neoantigen mRNA therapy in 1,137 resected high-risk melanoma patients: sequence tumor vs. normal DNA, algorithmically pick up to 34 neoantigens, encode them in patient-specific mRNA, and combine with Keytruda. Overall survival still being tracked; not yet approved.

entries.title: Higgsfield MCP + Claude — 3D websites to sell to local businesses
entries.creator: cevlocksin
entries.summary: Sponsored Higgsfield post: connect the Higgsfield MCP to Claude, find a local business with no website on Google Maps, paste its info into a prompt to generate an animated 3D site, then pitch it for $500. Income claims are promotional.

entries.title: Three OSINT tools — face-matched username search, exposed agents, world map
entries.creator: carterperez.dev
entries.summary: Teaser for three OSINT tools: a username search across 840 sites that also matches profile pictures to find accounts under other names, a scanner for AI agents companies left exposed online (and whether they touch company data), and a browser-based global intelligence live map you can self-host. Names gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Systems that prompt your AI — DB-driven loops with skills and cron
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Riffs on Boris Cherny's advice to build loops that prompt Claude instead of prompting it yourself: connect the AI to a database with work and issues tables, use cron jobs to detect pending changes, and run skills for scoping, implementing, testing and repeating until the human goal is met. Counterpoint: for go-to-market work the human is still the bottleneck and must stay in the loop.

entries.title: StopSlop — a Claude skill file that strips AI writing tells
entries.creator: therobertta
entries.summary: StopSlop is a GitHub skill file that bans filler phrases, throat-clearing openers, emphasis crutches and adverbs so Claude's copy stops sounding like Claude. The creator finds it removes most tells but notes the deeper problem: AI prose lacks a position, so the last 20% still needs a human voice.

entries.title: Claude Code Meta ads pipeline — Arcads API, Ads MCP and an Airtable swipe file
entries.creator: mr.paidsocial
entries.summary: Setup for having Claude Code generate and launch static Meta ads: clone the creator's GitHub repo in Claude Desktop's code tab, give it an Arcads.ai API key, add the Facebook/Meta Ads MCP as a custom connector, hand it an Airtable database of 2,000 example ads, have it ask 20 questions about your offer, pick 50 concepts, and upload creatives by cloning settings from an existing ad ID. Claims $30k revenue at 10-50 cents per image.

entries.title: Vibe-coded landing page toolkit — seven tools for real design taste
entries.creator: adam_ha_yes
entries.summary: Toolkit for better AI-built landing pages: 21st.dev components, getdesign.md to borrow famous design systems, WebGPU for heavy web animation, impeccable.style design prompts, a repo for recreating any landing page, awesome-design to break down brand design blocks, and a repo that 'gives Claude taste'. Last two repos are unnamed.

entries.title: Mixed-reality infinite canvas — directing Claude Code agents from Quest 3
entries.creator: rndyrbrts
entries.summary: Early demo of an XR infinite canvas on Meta Quest 3 synced with a desktop canvas: drop reference images into a sphere, put your hand in it and speak a request (e.g. components visualizing multi-agent progress), make a fist to send it to Claude Code agents under custom orchestration, and watch results build up in place.

entries.title: Claude Code simple mode — ablating system prompts makes the model smarter
entries.creator: foundedceo
entries.summary: Boris Cherny at YC Startup School: Claude Code accepts --system-prompt for a custom system prompt, and an undocumented simple mode (env var CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1) deletes all system and tool prompts. Anthropic uses it as an ablation and finds the model is slightly more intelligent without them, though product prompts still help it behave as users expect.

entries.title: Hugging Bay — torrent index for open LLM weights
entries.creator: wutronicai
entries.summary: Hugging Bay is a Pirate Bay-style site for downloading open model weights via BitTorrent, pairing with torrent CLIs to pull large models without hammering a single host.

entries.title: Attention-directing web design — spacing, contrast and pacing as persuasion
entries.creator: jerrythewebdev
entries.summary: Caption-only essay: premium websites control attention through spacing, contrast, motion and pacing, deciding what you notice, where you pause and when you click, which makes the brand feel more valuable and trustworthy. Mood reference; the video has no instructional audio.

entries.title: Nine UI design languages — feeding style guides to Manus
entries.creator: hustlewbill
entries.summary: Sponsored Manus post listing design languages used to vibe-code sites: skeuomorphism, neumorphism, glassmorphism, claymorphism, minimalism, maximalism, brutalism, liquid glass and spatial UI, fed as a design guide plus prompts to the Manus agent.

entries.title: Kimi K3 — hyped open-weight 2.8T model claims to beat Fable 5 cheaply
entries.creator: tenfoldmarc
entries.summary: Hype clip claiming Moonshot's Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters, open source) beat Claude Fable 5 on coding and design at ~5x lower cost, rattled the Nasdaq, and built a CS:GO portal clone for ~$3 in tokens. No benchmarks shown; link gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Claude Code website remix — clone and combine sites from URLs
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: Paste URLs of sites you like into Claude Code and ask it to clone and merge elements (Apple's animation, Stripe's pricing, Airbnb's design), then improve copy and add sections. Thin pitch; tutorial gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Prime Agent — self-rewriting harness lifts Opus 5 to 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3
entries.creator: wassimyounes_
entries.summary: Prime Intellect released Prime Agent, an open-source coding harness built on a Recursive Language Model (RLM) framework that rewrites its own prompts, memory, tasks and scaffolding at runtime based on failures. Opus 5 alone scores 30% on ARC-AGI-3; with the harness, 95.5%, a hair over the 95.4% human baseline. The real story is test-time compute and self-modifying scaffolding.

entries.title: Fully synthetic AI creator — Higgsfield, ElevenLabs, Veo and CapCut stack
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: How viral fake-influencer videos are made: generate the character in Higgsfield or Midjourney, voice it with ElevenLabs, animate with an AI video model like Veo or Runway, and stitch in CapCut. Useful as a pipeline map and as a detection primer.

entries.title: Kronos — transformer that reads candlesticks as a language (part 3)
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: Final part of a Kronos explainer: after binary spherical quantization and hierarchical encoding turn candles into tokens, a transformer uses self-attention (query/key/value per candle) to weight relevant bars like a volume spike over chop, and an autoregressive decoder predicts the next tokens, i.e. future price action. Contrasts with sequential LSTMs.

entries.title: Trojan-horse marketplace — co-marketing with adjacent vendors via AI
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Growth tactic from a former YC head of growth: have an AI app builder (Emergent) spin up a marketplace, find vendors selling to the same customers (not direct competitors), invite them to be featured, offer generous affiliate splits (10% to you, 20% to them), and use the relationship to land co-branded webinars and channel partnerships.

entries.title: Gemma Translator — offline speech translation on a Raspberry Pi 5
entries.creator: itsnicconley
entries.summary: Google open-sourced Gemma Translator: Moonshine for speech recognition, Gemma for translation and a TTS model for voice, all on a Raspberry Pi 5 with no network at ~7 tokens/sec, enough for live Spanish–Mandarin conversation. Repo includes code, parts list (battery, touchscreen, speaker, micro keyboard with language knob), deployment script and printable STL case.

entries.title: Liquid Death concert placements — AI-automated band seeding playbook
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Recreates Liquid Death's stunt with AI: list venues in a city, every band playing in the next two weeks into a table, generate can-friendly album art for custom-printed boxes, and mail bands free product so the can sits on stage in every photo. Address-finding step raises privacy concerns.

entries.title: Sherlock — install and run the top username OSINT tool with uv
entries.creator: carterperez.dev
entries.summary: Install Sherlock in three commands: create and activate a venv with uv, then uv pip install sherlock-project; run sherlock followed by one or more usernames to find matching accounts across the web.

entries.title: Flock plate-search transparency site — see which police searched you and why
entries.creator: carterperez.dev
entries.summary: A public website lets you enter a license plate and see which police departments ran Flock ALPR searches on it, browse a department's full search history, and read stated reasons (protest, theft, speeding). Flock reportedly sought a takedown that Cloudflare refused. Link gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Trending Claude resource repo — unnamed 60k-star collection
entries.creator: angelo_patsilivas
entries.summary: Teaser for a #1-trending GitHub repo (60k+ stars) collecting ready-made instructions, multi-step chains and a daily-updated feed of what top AI builders do; the repo isn't named in the post.

entries.title: Open-source object tracking — the tech inside Flock cameras, free
entries.creator: billy.coder
entries.summary: Repo Heist episode arguing the tracking behind $3k Flock cameras is free on GitHub: a 50k-star open-source library that detects, tracks and counts objects on any feed (doorbell, webcam, drone), demoed tracking every football player's speed, position and possession in one Python file. Repo name gated.

entries.title: Three OSINT tools — email account discovery, onion crawler, lookup suite
entries.creator: carterperez.dev
entries.summary: Teaser for three OSINT tools: one maps an email to every account it signed up for with name, photo and breach data; one crawls every site linked from an onion address into a searchable file; one bundles 20 terminal lookups (phone, Wi-Fi location, crypto wallet tracing, Sherlock). Names gated.

entries.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash re-post-training — big agentic gains, same model size
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: DeepSeek re-post-trained V4 Flash (284B MoE, ~13B active) with no size or architecture change, jumping Terminal Bench 2.1 from 61.8 to 82.7, past the V4 Pro preview and near Claude Opus 4.8, at $0.28 per million output tokens. V4's original recipe distilled 10+ specialist teacher models; V4 Pro (rumored 1.6T, 49B active) is next.

entries.title: AI search citations — why your chatbot cites the 'unlocked web'
entries.creator: wetclaude
entries.summary: High-credibility sites (Consumer Reports, ~60% of top news) block GPTBot, Google's AI crawler and Common Crawl, so AI search reads only what's left: AI-written pages and self-ranking listicles. One in six cited sources is AI-written and models often do post-hoc citation, writing the answer first and finding sources after.

entries.title: PPF Contact Solver — ZOZO's open-source GPU cloth and soft-body physics
entries.creator: marc.kaz
entries.summary: ZOZO open-sourced ppf-contact-solver, its internal virtual try-on physics engine: penetration-free fabric, rope and soft-body simulation with strain limits, up to 180M contacts, full GPU acceleration, a Blender plugin and a JupyterLab interface.

entries.title: Qwen 3.8 27B — local agentic model that fits on one 24GB GPU
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 27B quantizes to ~17GB at 4-bit, running on a single RTX 3090/4090, and Qwen's own benchmarks claim 84.3 on OSWorld plus wins on SWE-Bench Pro. Gated DeltaNet layers keep a compact running memory instead of full attention, and it preserves reasoning across tool-call steps, so pair it with an agent harness rather than chatting.

entries.title: Scroll-scrubbed product animation — Apple-style image sequence with AI
entries.creator: cindiezhu
entries.summary: Four-step recipe: generate start and end frames in Google Flow, animate between them with frames-to-video, export 30fps frames with Easy GIF, then have your AI coding tool build a scroll-linked canvas image sequence. Same trick Apple uses on product pages.

entries.title: OSINT recon trio — open databases, 135-check footprint, GitHub leak alerts
entries.creator: carterperez.dev
entries.summary: Three unnamed open-source OSINT tools: one finds exposed databases from a single domain, one runs 135 recon and security checks to map a company's attack surface, and one monitors GitHub commits for leaked API keys and passwords with Telegram alerts. Tool names are gated behind a comment-for-link.

entries.title: ASCILINE — 30fps video streamed as colored text over WebSockets
entries.creator: marc.kaz
entries.summary: ASCILINE converts real video server-side into binary-packed text sent over WebSockets, and the browser repaints colored block characters on a canvas at 360p/30fps. No video element, so it slips past video blockers and works on weak connections; frames can also be piped to local LLMs.

entries.title: Claude setup purge — audit stale CLAUDE.md rules for newer models
entries.creator: cooper.simson
entries.summary: Argues rules and skills written for older Claude models now hold newer ones back, citing Anthropic cutting much of its system prompt after Opus 5. Recommends a prompt that audits every CLAUDE.md rule and skill, deletes dead weight and rebuilds a lean setup; the prompt itself is comment-gated.

entries.title: Vibe-coded app performance — five fixes Claude usually skips
entries.creator: haydenschmitty
entries.summary: Five backend/frontend performance gaps in AI-written apps: uncompressed JSON responses, row-by-row database inserts, a single dependency bottleneck in round-trip latency, no optimistic UI updates, and server re-rendering HTML for every visitor instead of caching.

entries.title: Agent workspace file tree — persistent memory and context folder layout
entries.creator: cooper.simson
entries.summary: A folder structure for Claude-based agents: a brain folder with CLAUDE.md and model routing, five business context files, a memory folder with session logs and an index, per-project context files, NOW.md short-term memory, skills/workflows/scripts folders, Obsidian + GitHub versioning, Notion tasks, and secrets in a gitignored .env.

entries.title: Self-study pipeline — saved links to AI-generated study guides and quizzes
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Save videos and articles via Chrome extensions or text into a table, then give your agent a skill that groups recent saves by topic and generates study guides and quizzes, optionally through NotebookLM. Active recall instead of passive watching.

entries.title: Claude Code Meta ads — agent-run campaigns via Meta API repo
entries.creator: mr.paidsocial
entries.summary: A paid-social veteran recommends a ~1,100-star GitHub repo of skills that lets Claude Code run Meta ad campaigns through the Meta API: it walks you through API key setup, generates creatives and copy, and manages Ads Manager. Repo name is comment-gated; anecdotal ROAS claims.

entries.title: Grok Bot — persistent AI workers sharing one cloud computer
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: xAI's Grok Bot gives each user one dedicated cloud computer shared by all their bots, which can spawn long-lived bots, hand off work and switch underlying models. Docs warn bots share files, browser sessions and credentials, so they are not a security boundary.

entries.title: Vibe-coded app legal risks — ten compliance gaps that get you sued
entries.creator: murphmaxxing
entries.summary: Ten liability traps for indie apps with rough per-user fines: missing or incomplete privacy policy (data collection, AI use, third parties), undeleted uploads, public storage buckets, fake testimonials, hard-to-cancel subscriptions, silent trial auto-charges, and chatbots without self-harm handling.

entries.title: MacBook notch agent monitor — software answer to OpenAI's agent controller
entries.creator: cooper.simson
entries.summary: Instead of OpenAI's $230 hardware controller for babysitting coding agents, the creator had Claude build a MacBook notch app showing which agents are working, need attention or are done, with jump-to-session and permission approvals. Build guide is comment-gated.

entries.title: AI weekly roundup — Pocket TTS, Hermes Skills Hub, Kimi K3 in pure C
entries.creator: drcintas
entries.summary: Six releases: Kyutai Pocket TTS (100M-param local voice cloning, 6x real-time), Nous Research Hermes Skills Hub (90k agent skills), Grok Imagine Image 2.0 regional editing, Meta Muse Code terminal agent with parallel worktrees, Qwen3.8-Max (2.4T MoE, 1M context), and kimi-k3-in-c, a 176KB C99 engine streaming experts from disk to run a 2T model with no GPU.

entries.title: Evo-designed bacteriophages — AI genomes that beat human gene swaps
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: Science paper: researchers fine-tuned Evo 1 and Evo 2 on 14,466 phage sequences to generate PhiX174-like genomes, and 16 were viable. One (Evo 536) used a G4 packaging protein swap humans had failed to engineer, and recombined AI phages overcame E. coli resistance within 1-5 rounds. Visuals are illustrative, made with Seedance 2.5.

entries.title: Faceless horror channel pipeline — AI agent sourcing, human voice and edit
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Argues against fully AI faceless-channel courses: have an agent scrape a horror subreddit (with credit), generate clips with a video model, then hire a human narrator and editor (or use Descript). AI handles admin and sourcing, humans keep the creative part.

entries.title: Claude website design stack — Kowalski, Impeccable and taste skills plus MCP
entries.creator: nateherkai
entries.summary: Install the Emil Kowalski design and Impeccable skills for layout, type and motion, add a taste skill that pulls inspiration from real sites, then connect Figma MCP and Playwright so Claude can design, build and visually test websites.

entries.title: Bilevel autoresearch loops — an outer coach loop rewrites the search
entries.creator: raycfu
entries.summary: Builds on Karpathy's autoresearch loop (try change, test, keep or revert). An outer coach loop watches the inner worker and rewrites its search playbook so it stops repeating the same ideas; claimed ~5x better on Karpathy's benchmark with the same models.

entries.title: MiniMax H3 — unified multi-reference video model with open weights coming
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: MiniMax H3 generates 4-15s video at up to 2K with stereo sound, combining motion from a video, character from an image and voice from audio in one job. Uses contextual omni-representation training and the H3VAE tokenizer, regenerates low-res output at 2K from the original references, is on the MiniMax API, and weights are promised.

entries.title: Conway's Law — your product ships your org chart
entries.creator: shakib_hammad
entries.summary: Melvin Conway's 1967 observation: systems copy the communication structure of the organization that builds them. Modern teams apply the reverse Conway maneuver, designing the target architecture first and then shaping teams to match.

entries.title: Shell sort — gap-based insertion sort that moves items far early
entries.creator: algo.andre
entries.summary: Shell sort runs insertion sort on elements separated by a shrinking gap, letting small values travel long distances early. By the final gap-1 pass the list is nearly sorted, so insertion sort finishes quickly.

entries.title: AI weekly roundup — Codex Micro controller, LingBot-Map, robot MMA
entries.creator: stics.ai
entries.summary: Carousel of the week's AI news: OpenAI's $230 Codex Micro agent controller, China's robot MMA fight, Netflix using gen AI in ~300 productions, GPT-5.6 driving Blender via Blender MCP, open-source LingBot-Map building real-time 3D maps from video without LiDAR, free Claude for K-12 teachers, and Claude Fable 5 going permanent.

entries.title: AI subscriptions worth paying for — a founder's quick top-ten list
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Rapid-fire opinion list of AI-adjacent spend worth it: a better agent search tool, Gemini, Railway for hosting, Tesla, upgrading SaaS tiers for API/MCP access, Claude Fable 5, site analytics and Home Assistant over Google Home/Alexa. Mostly vibes, few specifics.

entries.title: Quantum reservoir computing — nine atoms forecasting weather
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: USTC researchers in Hefei built a quantum reservoir computer from nine interacting atoms that beat classical baselines on weather prediction. The reservoir needs no training, only the readout is trained, and quantum noise is used as the fading memory that time-series forecasting needs.

entries.title: Baidu Unlimited OCR — 3B local model parsing 100-page PDFs in one pass
entries.creator: ai.honeycove
entries.summary: Baidu's Unlimited OCR is a 3B-parameter, MIT-licensed model that reads whole documents (up to ~100 pages) in a single pass, preserving tables, headings, formulas and reading order. Runs locally, so it can replace a messy preprocessing stack in RAG and document-search pipelines.

entries.title: LLM identity confusion — Claude and Grok claim to be Chinese models
entries.creator: _dbrogle
entries.summary: Researchers queried four American LLMs via API without system prompts, in Chinese, about their identity. GPT and Gemini answered correctly, but Claude Opus 4.8 claimed to be Chinese (mostly Qwen) 60% of the time and Grok 97% (mostly DeepSeek), a likely trace of distillation-style synthetic training data.

entries.title: Cochlea — Wi-Fi side-channel attack on Ring cameras
entries.creator: bennjordan
entries.summary: Benn Jordan's Cochlea is a Python tool that runs on a Raspberry Pi with a monitor-mode Wi-Fi adapter and passively fingerprints encrypted traffic from cloud cameras like Ring. It detects when a camera sees motion and when the owner opens live view, logging to CSV, which shows how much activity leaks without breaking encryption.

entries.title: Motion editing website teaser — comment bait, no content
entries.creator: yukihasmotion
entries.summary: Comment-bait post for a motion-editing website with a one-word transcript and no named subject.

entries.title: Jacobian conjecture — AI-claimed counterexample explained via maps
entries.creator: ffppod
entries.summary: Explains the claim that an AI found a counterexample to the century-old Jacobian conjecture: whether a polynomial map with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant is always globally invertible. Walks through Jacobians as area ratios using the Mercator projection.

entries.title: Clipping economy — brands pay per-view for creator content reposts
entries.creator: cnn
entries.summary: CNN report on clipping: content-rewards platforms list campaigns from creators, brands and tourism boards, and clippers cut, caption and repost the footage for about $1-1.50 per thousand views. Top operators claim eight-figure revenue and pitch it as a pocket-sized billboard replacing traditional ad buys.

entries.title: Agentic OS on Claude Fable 5 — cron loop with earned autonomy
entries.creator: raycfu
entries.summary: Blueprint: a cron-run loop.sh where a cheap model triages changes, Fable 5 plans as manager, Sonnet executes and a fresh Fable reviews. Tasks earn autonomy after 20 passes at 95% and lose it below 90%, refusals come back as HTTP 200 so scripts must check stop_reason, and a goals directory reruns regression tests daily.

entries.title: DIY media brand — agent-written features and carousels instead of paid press
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Instead of paying for 'as seen on Forbes' features, have an agent DM influencers offering features, rewrite their top posts into articles with a humanizer repo, then turn articles into Instagram carousels with a carousel-generator repo and pitch collabs. Repo names and prompts are comment-gated.

entries.title: Humanizer skill for Claude Code — strip AI tells from your writing
entries.creator: jens.heitmann
entries.summary: Build one Claude Code skill from the blader/humanizer repo (based on Wikipedia's 'Signs of AI writing'), plus structural tells from the StoryScope paper and dataset. Wire it into CLAUDE.md rules and hooks so every human-facing doc gets a de-AI pass.

entries.title: Nvidia closed-loop cooling — why it grows demand for chillers
entries.creator: natestav
entries.summary: Nvidia's Rubin closed-loop liquid cooling removes evaporative water use but still needs chillers, heat exchangers, dry coolers and liquid cooling units. Modine (MOD), via its Airedale subsidiary, hit $1.1B data center revenue (+73%) and got $165M upfront from a hyperscaler. Read the engineering, not the headline sell-off.

entries.title: Elite flight signals — tracking how the ultra-wealthy hedge instability
entries.creator: jamiewheal
entries.summary: Three signals: a vibe-coded art project tracking oligarch private-jet departures, a Forbes report on villas, yachts and golden-visa demand, and Douglas Rushkoff's story of billionaires asking how to control security forces after 'the event'. Ends with a pitch for a paid leadership program.

entries.title: Car flipping agent — Facebook Marketplace MCP plus Kelley Blue Book
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Connect an AI agent to a Facebook Marketplace MCP tool, have it search your keywords each morning, compare listings against Kelley Blue Book using browser tools, message sellers and text you when something is below market. Split each step into a scheduled skill.

entries.title: Blender rigid-body spaceship — motors, constraints and drivers for flight
entries.creator: ianhubertz
entries.summary: Ian Hubert shows physics-driven vehicle animation in Blender: active/passive rigid bodies, hinge and spring constraints, motor constraints pushing against the ground as thrusters, gravity off, and custom properties wired via drivers with scripted expressions for throttle and lights. Mentions Erindale's XInputReader addon for gamepad control.

entries.title: Scroll World skill — one-shot animated scrolling websites
entries.creator: chase.h.ai
entries.summary: Scroll World is an open-source agent skill for Claude Fable 5 or GPT-5.6: describe a site, approve generated stills, and it turns them into video clips and stitches a scroll-animated page. The creator's fork adds mobile fixes and budget tiers for Higgsfield spend.

entries.title: Time complexity patterns — ten loop shapes to recognize in interviews
entries.creator: algomasterio
entries.summary: Cheat sheet mapping code shapes to Big-O: hash lookup O(1), halving loop O(log n), single and sequential loops O(n) and O(n+m), loop plus binary search and divide-and-conquer O(n log n), nested and triangular loops O(n²), branching recursion exponential, permutations O(n!).

entries.title: DIY fractional CFO — finance API sync plus AI analysis skills
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Sync transactions from a finance API into your own tables, then run agent prompts that categorize income and expenses, flag waste and spot under-investment, refining each into a reusable skill. Pitched as a replacement for a $15k fractional CFO.

entries.title: Liquid AI Antidoom — FTPO training to kill reasoning doom loops
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: Antidoom is Liquid AI's open-source pipeline that finds the exact token restarting a repetition loop, marks it rejected, picks up to 20 alternatives, and trains with Final Token Preference Optimization (FTPO) plus a KL-like regularizer in logit space so reasoning isn't damaged.

entries.title: Fable 5 plus GPT-5.6 routing — Codex plugin inside Claude Code
entries.creator: cooper.simson
entries.summary: Install Codex and the Codex plugin for Claude Code, then build a /route skill: Fable 5 interviews you and plans, GPT-5.6 executes, Fable reviews and loops until done. Splits usage across two subscriptions.

entries.title: Obsidian knowledge vault — viral 'Anthropic engineer brain' graph
entries.creator: ainewscentral
entries.summary: Viral claim that an Anthropic engineer's Obsidian vault (~8,900 nodes) is structured like a neural network and runs internal decisions. Unverified hype, but the underlying point is that disciplined markdown linking in Obsidian scales into a real knowledge graph.

entries.title: Nintendo static recompilation — native Zelda and Mario Kart ports
entries.creator: quickfinesse
entries.summary: Static recompilation projects turn Switch games into native apps: Tears of the Kingdom on Apple Silicon Mac and iPhone (~90fps on a MacBook Air), Skyward Sword HD on Windows, Linux, Steam Deck and Mac at 60fps/4K with a mod manager, and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on iPhone/Mac with online play. Bring your own game copy.

entries.title: Identity (2025) — Malayalam crime thriller about memory and sketch art
entries.creator: hollywoodwatchers
entries.summary: Movie card for Identity, a Malayalam action-thriller where a sketch artist and an officer work from a witness with photographic memory; on ZEE5, IMDb ~7.4. The attached audio is an unrelated comedy sketch, so only the caption describes the film.

entries.title: Hoffman's interface theory — perception as a desktop, not reality
entries.creator: everythingplaybook
entries.summary: Podcast clip on Donald Hoffman's evolutionary game theory result: agents that perceive more than fitness payoffs lose to agents tuned only to reward, so perception works like desktop icons that hide the underlying machinery. Spacetime as interface, not ground truth.

entries.title: Glenn Gould's humming — thinking music away from the piano
entries.creator: dailyhistoryclips
entries.summary: Glenn Gould hummed audibly on nearly every recording despite Columbia engineers' mic tricks. He traced it to practising under a vacuum cleaner's noise, which taught him to hear pieces internally and learn away from the instrument; the voice is the overflow, audible on the Goldberg Variations.

entries.title: Untitled "xy + t" clip — no identifiable subject
entries.creator: bradleytangonan
entries.summary: Caption reads only 'xy + t' with no speech or OCR; no identifiable subject.

entries.title: Artist resources teaser — favorites never named
entries.creator: anngee.foote.creations
entries.summary: Artist shares 'favorite resources' but neither caption nor audio names any of them.

entries.title: Genie integer overflow — wishing for negative wishes
entries.creator: detroitanimations
entries.summary: 2D animated skit where a user exploits a genie's 2-bit wish counter: wishing for negative wishes should underflow to the maximum value, so he first upgrades the data type to 64 bits and ends with ~18 quintillion wishes. A fun explainer of integer overflow.

entries.title: Database Detective — solve crimes by writing SQL queries
entries.creator: frostechgmz
entries.summary: Database Detective is a Steam game where you solve absurd police cases by querying tables with SELECT, WHERE and JOIN to rule out suspects. Beginner-friendly with a manual, clear errors and a hint assistant, and it trains asking the right data question first. English only.

entries.title: The Wrong Game — clown exercise to break perceptual autopilot
entries.creator: clowndaddypresents
entries.summary: Point at an object and confidently name something it isn't. A 30-second clown warm-up that jolts attention, imagination and willingness to be wrong; stumbling or going blank counts as finding the clown.

entries.title: Bot Crossing — video-game workspace for managing 80 AI agents
entries.creator: jarrenrocks
entries.summary: Open-source game UI where AI agents live on a little planet, walk around, and raise their hands when they need help; click one to see its request. Built by Jarren Rocks, with a GitHub repo, YouTube build review and botcrossing.com site.

entries.title: LLM text watermarking — how token-bias watermarks work
entries.creator: chase.h.ai
entries.summary: Explains statistical watermarking: the model subtly reweights next-token probabilities with a secret key so a detector holding the key can spot the pattern over long outputs. Claims Claude Fable 5.1 watermarks everything and pitches a full-rewrite removal prompt; the claims are unverified.

entries.title: Marble extendable round dining table — 6-10 seat furniture design
entries.creator: mmtable_jacksonxu
entries.summary: Product clip of a round marble dining table that extends from 100-120 cm to 150-180 cm to seat 6-10. Furniture seller promo with no narration.

entries.title: Y-Pan — 3D-printed panoramic 35mm camera instead of a $5k XPan
entries.creator: plumsojuyang
entries.summary: A maker designed the Y-Pan, a 3D-printed panoramic film camera reproducing the Hasselblad XPan's wide 35mm format. Everything except the lens is printed, parts cost about $100, it builds in about a week, and the CAD files and bill of materials are on the creator's site.

entries.title: Grace Hopper 1982 — the value of information as a design constraint
entries.creator: mit_csail
entries.summary: MIT CSAIL clip of Grace Hopper predicting that data volume will grow faster than linearly and so will demand for instant access, and that the two conflict. Her answer: systems must understand the value of the information they process.

entries.title: Tristan Perich's 1-Bit Symphony — music from on/off pulses on a chip
entries.creator: egapmada
entries.summary: 1-Bit Symphony is a composition housed in a CD case: a microchip running assembly code that outputs 1-bit on/off pulses as sound. A 695-page companion book prints the processor's cycles for the first hundredth of a second.

entries.title: Artist Grant — $1,200 unrestricted grant with no proposal
entries.creator: creativeflairhq
entries.summary: Artist Grant awards $1,200 unrestricted to one visual artist three times a year since 2017. Apply by email with a website link or 3-5 images plus a short bio; $30 fee, visual arts only, open worldwide to 18+, past winners ineligible.

entries.title: Print-on-demand art prints — sell paintings with no stock or upfront cost
entries.creator: creativeflairhq
entries.summary: Upload photos to Printful, Gelato or Fine Art America, set a price, and they print, pack and ship while you keep the margin. The real work is the photo: flat, window daylight, no flash, straight on, cropped to the canvas, and list at least ten pieces.

entries.title: OSINT tools — photo geolocation, exposed AI servers, leak search
entries.creator: carterperez.dev
entries.summary: Three unnamed open-source OSINT tools: one geolocates photos without metadata, one scans the internet for unauthenticated AI servers and scores their exposure on a globe, and one searches leaked logins, wallets and dark web mentions by name or company. Links are comment-gated.

entries.title: Nagarjuna and Rovelli — emptiness meets relational quantum mechanics
entries.creator: thinkitthrough411
entries.summary: Carlo Rovelli devotes a chapter of Helgoland to Nagarjuna's Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way: nothing has independent existence, only relations. That mirrors Rovelli's relational interpretation where objects have properties only relative to other objects.

entries.title: Autonomous AI pentest agent — plain-English prompt to verified exploit
entries.creator: evenedsteven
entries.summary: An unnamed ~600-star GitHub repo where you describe a target in one sentence and an agent finds a vulnerability, runs the exploit and writes the report, across 13 AI providers. Every claimed finding is verified against real tool output. Authorized targets only.

entries.title: Sharp Memory Display — per-pixel memory LCD for low-power hardware
entries.creator: mewtru
entries.summary: Sharp memory displays store each pixel's state, so they only need a tiny maintenance signal. That makes them near e-paper in power, reflective for sunlight readability, yet fast enough for ~50fps, as on the Playdate.

entries.title: Orbiter — open-source smartphone 3D scanner for print-ready parts
entries.creator: rawmechatronics
entries.summary: Orbiter is an open-source rig and workflow from Raw Mechatronics for accurate 3D digitization with a smartphone camera. Scan an object, design around it and print a part that fits the first time.

entries.title: DIY founder PR — agent-scraped journalist requests and tailored pitches
entries.creator: angus.sewell
entries.summary: Have an agent scrape journalist request sites into a database, pull each journalist's last ten articles, draft a similar story angle featuring you, and send short emails. Lessons: short non-AI-sounding pitches win, offer visibility, do ideation yourself, claim your Google profile, and it's a volume game.

entries.title: Peppa Cam — DIY Raspberry Pi handheld LiDAR scanner
entries.creator: peppes_ghost
entries.summary: A homemade handheld LiDAR scanner from a Raspberry Pi, a LiDAR sensor and a 3D-printed housing, mapping buildings, caves, gardens and trees without proprietary software. Build plan with wiring, code and CAD is comment-gated.

entries.title: Hand-cut kitchen tile mosaic — materials and process from a first build
entries.creator: emils.salmins
entries.summary: First hand-cut mosaic: 2x2 cm Winckelmans tiles cut with two nippers, glued to fiberglass mesh with Titebond, mounted on Knauf Aquapanel with Mapei Adesilex P10, cured 30 hours, brown grout, and a 5mm silicone expansion gap. Took a month, not two weeks.

entries.title: Ozymandias read by Werner Herzog — archive and decay as film theme
entries.creator: sandboxfilms
entries.summary: Werner Herzog reads Shelley's 'Ozymandias' as the hook for Sandbox Films' documentary 'The Arc of Oblivion', about why humans build records that will inevitably fade. Worth it as a study in voice, pacing and pairing classic text with documentary imagery.

entries.title: Elizabeth Greenshields Foundation — no-deadline CAD 17k grant for early painters
entries.creator: creativeflairhq
entries.summary: The Elizabeth Greenshields Foundation gives CAD 17,000 first grants (20,000 on renewal) to early-career representational artists worldwide, with no fee, no CV and rolling applications by post. The Awesome Foundation's $1,000 monthly micro-grants (US, UK, Australia, Canada chapters) are the fallback for abstract or non-painting work.

entries.title: Cozy multiplayer browser game — open-world mail delivery on a tiny planet
entries.creator: setupspawn
entries.summary: An unnamed free browser game where you customize a character and deliver messages across a small Japanese-street-styled planet, with live multiplayer. Fun as a reference for what WebGL in the browser can do, but the post never names the site.
