entries.title: Turing patterns — why reaction-diffusion gives us five fingers
entries.creator: ri_science
entries.summary: Philip Ball (Royal Institution talk) explains that digit count is set during embryonic development by Alan Turing's 1952 reaction-diffusion mechanism: interacting chemical signals self-organize into regular stripes that become fingers. The Whisper transcript is garbled, so the caption and the known Turing model carry the content.

entries.title: The NeverEnding Story — the Nothing as a metaphor for lost hope
entries.creator: 90skidlibrary
entries.summary: A clip from The NeverEnding Story (1984) where the Nothing is explained as the despair left when people abandon their dreams, because people without hope are easy to control. Nostalgia and mood reference, no technique.

entries.title: DeepPIV laser-sheet scanning — 3D models of deep-sea siphonophores in situ
entries.creator: howtown_videos
entries.summary: Schmidt Ocean Institute's ROV on the Falkor (too) uses MBARI's DeepPIV system: a laser flattened into a thin sheet is swept through semi-transparent animals to capture planes that stack into full 3D reconstructions, without killing the specimen. The subject is a siphonophore, a colony of specialized zooids acting as one animal.

entries.title: Crystal Pite's The Seasons' Canon — contemporary ballet of mass ensemble motion
entries.creator: dima.easyart
entries.summary: Crystal Pite's 'The Seasons' Canon' (Paris Opera Ballet, 2016, set to Max Richter's Vivaldi recomposition), back at Palais Garnier. Worth studying for how a large ensemble moves as one organism.

entries.title: Jim Simons and the Riemann Hypothesis — the benchmark for AI math claims
entries.creator: ffppod
entries.summary: Anecdote about Renaissance Technologies founder Jim Simons lighting up when asked if he'd trade his fortune to solve the Riemann Hypothesis, used to argue that RH has become the gold-standard test people demand of AI math systems. Light commentary, no technical depth.

entries.title: HFT short-term reversal — buy weekly losers, sell winners across 4,500 stocks
entries.creator: 7am.research
entries.summary: A 60 Minutes clip with Manoj Narang describing a cross-sectional mean-reversion test: buy $5 of stocks down 5% last week, sell $10 of stocks up 10%, across the whole ~4,500-stock universe at once. Near 50% win rate per trade but no losing month thanks to breadth and speed, with Joe Saluzzi arguing it rigs the game.

entries.title: Efficiency-ratio forecaster — skip choppy days to lift a strategy's metrics
entries.creator: telonicstrading
entries.summary: Instead of predicting direction, a logistic regression on 15 price features forecasts the next day's Kaufman efficiency ratio (trendiness versus chop). Trades on predicted low-efficiency days made about a third of the money, so gating them out improved nearly every metric and held on two years of out-of-sample data.

entries.title: Overnight vs intraday returns — Knuteson's 'Strikingly Suspicious' anomaly
entries.creator: quantpapers
entries.summary: Bruce Knuteson (ex-MIT physicist, D. E. Shaw) splits each day into close-to-open and open-to-close: Micron since 1990 is +138M% overnight and -99.9% intraday, and the same sawtooth shows in 21 indices (China reversed). His paper 'Strikingly Suspicious Overnight and Intraday Returns' rejects earnings and news as explanations and alleges large firms push prices at the open; it's a claim, not a proof.

entries.title: PBEMA TradingView indicator — trend-filter buy/sell line on the S&P 500
entries.creator: pb_ema
entries.summary: Promo for a free TradingView indicator (PBEMA): buy when price is above a moving-average line, sell below, claimed to outperform buy-and-hold on the S&P 500 since 1930 by sidestepping 2000 and 2008. The Munger attribution and the personal P&L claims are unverified, and the link is gated behind a comment.

entries.title: 2010 Flash Crash — how Navinder Sarao spoofed E-mini S&P futures
entries.creator: thestockguytwitch
entries.summary: Story of the May 6, 2010 Flash Crash (about 9% in minutes, $1T wiped then recovered), traced to Navinder Sarao spoofing E-mini S&P 500 futures from his bedroom with large sell orders he cancelled, tricking algos into selling. Good primer on spoofing and cascading algorithmic selling.

entries.title: Claude multi-agent trading team — research, market, backtest and risk agents
entries.creator: raycfu
entries.summary: Pitch for an unnamed free repo that spins Claude into a four-agent trading team: a research agent cleans market data, a market agent writes strategy logic, a test agent backtests for win rate and max drawdown, and a risk agent audits for self-deception. The repo is never named; the link is gated behind a comment.

entries.title: Charlie Munger's inversion — solve problems by asking how to cause failure
entries.creator: charliemungerhub
entries.summary: Munger explains inversion with his WWII meteorologist job: ask how you'd kill pilots (icing, running out of fuel), then avoid those. Same move for any problem: list what would hurt it most and steer clear.

entries.title: Katsuyama vs BATS on CNBC — the 'markets are rigged' HFT showdown
entries.creator: itsfinancenote
entries.summary: The March 31, 2014 CNBC clash where IEX's Brad Katsuyama (Flash Boys) accused exchanges of selling HFT advantages via direct feeds, co-location and complex order types, and BATS's Bill O'Brien was pressed on whether his matching engine priced off the slower SIP. BATS later corrected the record, and IEX's speed bump came out of this debate.

entries.title: Chip stock selloff rumor — a fund blowup and the Intel overhang
entries.creator: thetradingfraternity
entries.summary: Market chatter tying a recent chip-stock selloff to a fund blowup by a trader famous for an Intel bet, with Ken Griffin reportedly absorbing the book off-market. Unsourced rumor plus generic macro commentary (yen, CDS, Kevin Warsh).

entries.title: Kronos — open-source foundation model trained on 12B candlesticks
entries.creator: gigaqian
entries.summary: Survey of zero-shot time-series foundation models (Google TimesFM 2.5, Amazon Chronos, Salesforce Moirai, IBM Tiny Time Mixers) that mostly fail at stock prediction, then Kronos: an open-source model pre-trained on about 12 billion K-lines from crypto and other markets that beats prior models on financial forecasting. Code on GitHub and Hugging Face from shiyu-coder.

entries.title: Warsh, the Clarity Act and tokenized stocks — crypto-rails news roundup
entries.creator: alexanderelorenzo
entries.summary: Hype-framed roundup: Kevin Warsh confirmed as Fed chair, the Clarity Act clearing Senate Banking 15-9, NYSE using Securitize for tokenized stocks, Nasdaq tokenizing the Russell 1000 and BlackRock filing tokenized funds. Ends in a comment-for-training funnel, so verify each claim yourself.

entries.title: Bollinger Bands + RSI kid trader — satire of trading-course culture
entries.creator: thestockguytwitch
entries.summary: Comedy skit mocking influencer trading courses: a 'first-grader' fumbles a Bollinger Bands plus RSI setup and still hits take-profit. Entertainment, not instruction.

entries.title: Quant/ML project reel — repo links gated, no content
entries.creator: tuba.captures
entries.summary: Silent reel with a 'comment Repo' caption and no transcript, OCR or named projects.

entries.title: Fundrise VCX at 25x NAV — cheaper proxies for private AI and space names
entries.creator: linalikesmoney
entries.summary: Fundrise's newly listed VCX closed-end fund trades around 25x its net asset value (about a 2,000% premium). Cheaper exposures named instead: Kraken Robotics as an Anduril supplier, Amazon for its Anthropic stake, and a Canadian private-asset fund near 1x NAV for OpenAI and SpaceX exposure.

entries.title: Regular Show's 'Synth Wars' — synthesizer battle as cosmic boss fight
entries.creator: electronicmusic.official
entries.summary: The climax of Regular Show's 'Gary's Synthesizer', where two half-brothers settle a throne dispute with a synth battle (discord vs harmony) that escalates into a cosmic boss fight. Fun reference for music-driven animated set pieces.

entries.title: Yi Jian Mei (一剪梅) — classic Mandarin ballad as a Chinese lesson
entries.creator: learnchinesewithyuna
entries.summary: A sing-along of the classic Mandarin ballad 'Yi Jian Mei' (A Spray of Plum Blossoms) used to teach Chinese. Slow, melodic lines make it a good pronunciation and tone drill.

entries.title: Ba Fang Lai Cai (八方来财) — viral Mandarin track for learners
entries.creator: elianxchina
entries.summary: 'Ba Fang Lai Cai' ('wealth from all directions'), a viral Chinese track with dense, rhythmic lyrics, shared as Mandarin learning material for Spanish-speaking learners.

entries.title: Dolly Parton's family sings 'In the Pines' — Appalachian roots on TV, 1977
entries.creator: unforgettableconcerts
entries.summary: On her 1977 variety show, Dolly Parton brought her parents and seven siblings on to sing 'In the Pines', the Appalachian folk song they grew up singing in East Tennessee. A rare look at the family harmony tradition underneath her career.

entries.title: Heather Mullein Hannah live at the Purple Fiddle — roots show thank-you
entries.creator: heather_mullein_hannah
entries.summary: A short thank-you clip from a Heather Mullein Hannah show at the Purple Fiddle with her band, with almost no audible music in the transcript. Mood reference only.

entries.title: 'Lonely USA' by Meels — banjo folk songwriting sketch
entries.creator: meelsmusic
entries.summary: A short banjo-backed original folk song about leaving 'Lonesome Town' for 'Kindred City'. A small songwriting reference for plainspoken Americana lyrics.

entries.title: Technotronic 'Pump Up the Jam' on SNL 1990 — hip-house goes mainstream
entries.creator: technoandhousemusic
entries.summary: Technotronic's 1990 Saturday Night Live performance of 'Pump Up the Jam', the house, hip-hop and Belgian new beat crossover that hit No. 2 in the US and UK. A time capsule of club music breaking into the mainstream.

entries.title: The Highwaymen live 1985 — Cash, Jennings, Nelson, Kristofferson supergroup
entries.creator: outlawcountrynews
entries.summary: Early live performance of 'Highwayman' by The Highwaymen, the 1985 outlaw-country supergroup of Johnny Cash, Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson and Kris Kristofferson. The song's four reincarnation verses, one per singer, are the structural trick.

entries.title: Born From Culture: Aotearoa — Māori haka film cut to Kendrick Lamar's N95
entries.creator: jamesmfenwick
entries.summary: James Fenwick's short film celebrating Māori culture through haka, waiata and whakapapa, made with Te Pā Tū, Mitai Māori Village and Whakarewarewa and cut to Kendrick Lamar's 'N95'. Strong reference for culture-led brand filmmaking with collaborators credited.

entries.title: AURORA's 'Rasputin' cover — disco classic reborn as dark folk ballad
entries.creator: globalvocaltalent
entries.summary: AURORA slows Boney M.'s 'Rasputin' to a sparse, ethereal arrangement with soft vocals and minimal instruments, turning a disco anthem into dark folk. A clear case study in reharmonizing mood without changing lyrics.

entries.title: 'Swannanoa Town' — Julie Boone's Appalachian tune at The Palace, Yancey County
entries.creator: murphydoesnotmatter
entries.summary: A performance of 'Swannanoa Town' (as played by the musician's relative, Julie Boone) filmed at The Palace in Yancey County, North Carolina. Traditional western North Carolina repertoire with a family lineage.

entries.title: Passion Pit's 'Sleepyhead' — sampling Mary O'Hara's 1958 Irish lullaby
entries.creator: baauer
entries.summary: Baauer breaks down how Passion Pit's 2008 'Sleepyhead' is built on a sample of Mary O'Hara's 1958 recording of the Irish lullaby 'Óró Mo Bháidín'. Great example of finding sample gold in old folk records.

entries.title: Bass khaen in A minor — the 190 cm Lao free-reed mouth organ
entries.creator: jerem.khaen
entries.summary: A short demo of a 190 cm bass khaen, the Lao/Isan bamboo free-reed mouth organ, tuned to A minor. Interesting timbre and drone reference.

entries.title: The Holler Hounds — 'War in the Homeland' southern-gothic country
entries.creator: thehollerhounds
entries.summary: A short southern-gothic country song by The Holler Hounds about a war in the homeland. Mood reference for Appalachian alt-country.

entries.title: 'Shady Grove' — Doc Watson's clawhammer D-Dorian and a 400-year melody
entries.creator: chancemccoymusic
entries.summary: Chance McCoy plays Doc Watson's clawhammer banjo 'Shady Grove' in modal D-Dorian (pull-offs, drop-thumb at speed) and traces the minor melody to Jean Ritchie's father in Viper, Kentucky, and back to Child Ballad #81, 'Matty Groves'. A deep lineage lesson in one tune.

entries.title: Bass talharpa improv — bowed Nordic lyre for cinematic drones
entries.creator: channing.watson
entries.summary: Improvisation on a newly finished bass talharpa (tagelharpa), the bowed Nordic lyre, by luthier-musician Channing Watson. Raw, droning cinematic texture.

entries.title: 'The Rocky Road to Dublin' — Irish sing-along tradition
entries.creator: songss
entries.summary: A group sing of 'The Rocky Road to Dublin', the fast slip-jig Irish ballad everyone knows by heart. Nostalgia piece; the 9/8 rhythm is the interesting bit.

entries.title: Johanna Wacker — queer country night promo at The Camel RVA
entries.creator: johannawacker
entries.summary: Promo for a queer country and roots show at The Camel in Richmond, Virginia, with Pet Names and Haley Ellis. Event post with a short clip.

entries.title: Johanna Wacker clawhammer — countdown to queer roots night in Richmond
entries.creator: johannawacker
entries.summary: Second promo for the same queer country and roots night at The Camel RVA, this one with a short clawhammer banjo clip.

entries.title: honeycrush 'My Dog' — DIY folk-horror video shot in Brooklyn
entries.creator: honeycrush.online
entries.summary: honeycrush's 'My Dog', a folk-horror tinged song about pursuit and cyclical love, longing and loathing, with a video shot entirely DIY by two people with one camera. Reference for low-budget music video mood.

entries.title: 'Sally in the Garden' — Crockett's Kentucky Mountaineers' 1929 modal tune
entries.creator: chancemccoymusic
entries.summary: Chance McCoy traces 'Sally in the Garden' to the Crockett Family Mountaineers' 1929 Brunswick 78 (Brunswick 291), a West Virginia fiddling family that drove a Model T to California and became 'California's first country stars'. A minor modal oddity among breakdowns, related to the Ozark 'Hog-Eye Man' tunes and Marion Sumner's driving version.

entries.title: 'The Winner Takes It All' in Mandarin — Lilith Liu's ABBA adaptation
entries.creator: lilithsomething
entries.summary: Lilith Liu sings ABBA's 'The Winner Takes It All' with her own Chinese lyrics. Example of lyric translation that keeps melody and emotional arc.

entries.title: Banjo mantra in gDFAD — D-minor clawhammer drone
entries.creator: winterkendl
entries.summary: A meditative clawhammer banjo piece in D minor using the gDFAD tuning, recorded while clearing a woodland trail. Handy tuning reference for modal banjo.

entries.title: From China to Appalachia — Cathy Fink, Chao Tian and Marcy Marxer tour
entries.creator: cfinkbanjo
entries.summary: Tour promo for Cathy Fink, Marcy Marxer and Chao Tian's 'From China to Appalachia' project blending Chinese and old-time music, teasing 'Jasmine Flower'. Mostly dates, little music.

entries.title: 'Long Night Ahead' — Irish tavern song written for D&D sessions
entries.creator: colmrmcguinness
entries.summary: Colm R. McGuinness's original drinking song inspired by Dungeons & Dragons, built as a counting, escalating tavern chorus. Ready-made bard material for tabletop sessions.

entries.title: 'The Cuckoo' on fretless clawhammer banjo — Appalachian standard
entries.creator: johannawacker
entries.summary: Johanna Wacker plays and sings 'The Cuckoo' on fretless banjo in clawhammer style. A core old-time tune; fretless gives the slides and bluesy intonation.

entries.title: Dance in Guilin, China — blue-toned closing performance clip
entries.creator: sea_ving
entries.summary: A short dance performance filmed in Guilin, China, framed with a blue color grade as a closing piece. Visual mood reference, no audible music detail.

entries.title: Tolkien's dwarf song on octave mandolin — Lady Moon for Eastman
entries.creator: eastmanguitars
entries.summary: Lady Moon sings the Hobbit's 'That's What Bilbo Baggins Hates' on her Eastman signature octave mandolin for Tolkien Reading Day. Brand promo, but a nice reference for setting Tolkien verse to folk accompaniment.

entries.title: 'Rivers and Roads' instrumental — The Head and the Heart cover clip
entries.creator: chance.s.emerson
entries.summary: A short instrumental take on The Head and the Heart's 'Rivers and Roads', part of a 'spinny thing' series. Little to study beyond the song choice.

entries.title: Cookie-tin fretless banjo — a DIY instrument built with a parent
entries.creator: johannawacker
entries.summary: Johanna Wacker plays clawhammer on a fretless banjo she built from a cookie tin with her dad, singing the old-time 'railroad man' hen verses. Proof that a tin-can body makes a usable, bright-sounding banjo.

entries.title: Ievan Polkka in Russian — the Finnish polka with new lyrics
entries.creator: kvashenaya
entries.summary: A Russian-language version of the 'Finnish polka' (Ievan Polkka), keeping the story of Eva dancing against her mother's wishes and the nonsense scat chorus. Shows how a folk dance tune travels across languages.

entries.title: 'Irish Eyes' by Rose Betts — Isabel Dumaa's a cappella cover
entries.creator: isabeldumaa
entries.summary: Isabel Dumaa sings Rose Betts's 'Irish Eyes', a modern folk song built on a repeated 'my mother says / my father says' inheritance structure. Clean vocal reference for St Patrick's season.

entries.title: 'Oo-De-Lally' from Disney's Robin Hood — Roger Miller cover
entries.creator: isabeldumaa
entries.summary: Isabel Dumaa covers Roger Miller's 'Oo-De-Lally' from Disney's 1973 Robin Hood. Light nostalgic cover, no arrangement twist.

entries.title: 'Irish Eyes' cover repost — remix of Isabel Dumaa's version
entries.creator: iamodnp
entries.summary: A repost/remix of Isabel Dumaa's cover of Rose Betts's 'Irish Eyes', the same performance saved separately in this batch.

entries.title: 'Shady Grove' — from Renaissance ballad to Appalachian standard
entries.creator: seanofthesouth
entries.summary: Sean of the South sings 'Shady Grove' and notes it crossed the Atlantic as a Renaissance-era song before Appalachia turned it into an American tune. Full verses (Barlow knife, big fine horse, bare feet) make it a good lyric reference.

entries.title: Techno subgenres explained — melodic, acid, minimal and hard techno
entries.creator: special.ray_
entries.summary: A visual guide contrasting techno subgenres (melodic, hard, acid, minimal) by feel and energy, from a techno playlist creator. Caption-level overview; the transcript has no detail.

entries.title: Gus Tritsch 'Lonely' — The Wild Shoats string-band fiddle tune
entries.creator: thewildshoats
entries.summary: Short clip of Gus Tritsch's 'Lonely' from The Wild Shoats, promoting their album 'Great American Novel'. Full video lives on YouTube.

entries.title: Gigamesh's Radiohead house cover — release teaser
entries.creator: gigamesh
entries.summary: Teaser for Gigamesh's house-music reworking of a Radiohead song, with no audio detail captured. Release promo.

entries.title: Weevils Trio 'December's High' — climate crisis told as a Colorado wildfire
entries.creator: weevilstrio
entries.summary: Claire of Weevils Trio performs 'December's High', a fiddle-led song about the global climate crisis disguised as a story about a disastrous Colorado wildfire. Good model for making a big topic land through one local story.

entries.title: The khaen — Lao bamboo free-reed organ that plays on inhale and exhale
entries.creator: pop.music.culture
entries.summary: Explainer on the khaen from Laos and Isan: bamboo pipes with metal free reeds, played by both blowing and drawing breath like a harmonica, so it can sustain continuous sound and simple chords. Its buzzing, hypnotic tone now shows up in electronic and ambient music.
